question.text: Two cells with the same e.m.f. \(E\) and different internal resistances \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) are connected in series to an external resistance \(R\). The value of \(R\) so that the potential difference across the first cell be zero is

solution.text:
Hints:
\(I=\frac{2 E}{R+r_1+r_2}\) Potential difference across first cell \(\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{E}-\mathrm{Ir}_1=0\) \(\begin{aligned} & E-\frac{2 E r_1}{R+r_1+r_2}=0 \\ & {\left[\frac{R+r_1+r_2-2 r_1}{R+r_1+r_2}\right]=0} \\ & \Rightarrow R+r_2-r_1=0 \\ & R=r_1-r_2 \end{aligned}\)
